name_zh: 相位与动作幅度的可识别分解
formal_object: A smooth legal trajectory Y(t), small phase offsets tau in a fixed endpoint-preserving basis, amplitude basis B; desired model/input-derived residual r; P is the phase Jacobian.

operations.condition: Smooth trajectory and small monotone time warp

operations.input: Weighted least squares in phase and amplitude blocks
operations.condition: Unconstrained phase elimination only when no phase inequality is active

operations.input: Overlap of phase and amplitude spans
operations.condition: Jacobian rank and gauge are checked
gauge-aware phase subspace; full-column-rank amplitude basis; inactive inequalities
operations.output: kappa separation, sharp noise amplification and ridge/data-identifiability distinction

derivation_steps.statement: Linearize the repair as r approximately P xi+B gamma, with phase endpoint offsets zero.
derivation_steps.justification: Taylor expansion in a declared small phase basis.

derivation_steps.statement: Let M=I-P(P^T W P)^dagger P^T W; after unconstrained phase elimination, gamma*=(B^T W M B+lambda I)^-1 B^T W M r.
derivation_steps.justification: Weighted Schur elimination and ridge least squares.

derivation_steps.statement: For monotone time, impose 1+tau'(t)>0; if the bound is active, solve the full constrained block problem instead of the unconstrained formula.
derivation_steps.justification: Elimination formula does not silently enforce inequality constraints.

derivation_steps.statement: Overlapping phase/amplitude directions are unidentifiable without extra constraints; residual second-order error is O(||tau||^2).
derivation_steps.justification: Rank deficiency and the retained Taylor remainder limit the claim.

derivation_steps.statement: Let L=W^(1/2), U span range(LP), M0=I-UU^T, and LB=VR with V^T V=I and R invertible. The amplitude data curvature in eta=R gamma is S=V^T M0 V=I-V^T UU^T V.
derivation_steps.justification: Whiten and eliminate the unconstrained phase block; thin QR requires B full column rank. Gauge redundancy in P is removed or treated as a subspace.

derivation_steps.statement: kappa=lambda_min(S)=1-sigma_max(U^T V)^2; with no phase subspace define the cross singular value as zero. kappa>0 iff M0 V has full column rank.
derivation_steps.justification: S=(M0 V)^T(M0 V); use the largest eigenvalue of V^T UU^T V. The result is invariant to changes of phase basis.

derivation_steps.statement: For kappa>0 and zero ridge, ||Delta eta||<=||e||/sqrt(kappa), and ||Delta gamma||<=||R^-1|| ||e||/sqrt(kappa), for whitened residual perturbation e.
derivation_steps.justification: eta=(M0 V)^+ M0 rbar. The minimum singular value is sqrt(kappa); its left singular vectors lie in range(M0), giving the exact worst-direction operator norm.

derivation_steps.statement: If Bv=Pu!=0, (xi,gamma) and (xi-au,gamma+av) predict identically. Positive amplitude ridge can make its profiled inverse exist without identifying the true decomposition from data.
derivation_steps.justification: The two changes cancel algebraically. This ambiguity concerns an interior/inactive-inequality problem; active monotonicity or boundary constraints may remove specific aliases.

derivation_steps.statement: For original t_j and piecewise-linear internal tau, impose tau_(j+1)-tau_j>=-(1-m)(t_(j+1)-t_j), m>0, and zero endpoint offsets.
derivation_steps.justification: Each warped interval has positive slope at least m. Higher-order interpolation needs segment-interior derivative qualification, not just node ordering.

derivation_steps.statement: For block-diagonal W=diag(w_i I) and ||Y_i second derivative||<=K_i, ||epsilon_linear||_W<=.5 sqrt(sum_i w_i K_i^2 tau_i^4).
derivation_steps.justification: Pointwise Taylor remainder followed by weighted Euclidean aggregation. The formula is not asserted for arbitrary off-diagonal W; decomposition can amplify this residual near kappa=0.

assumptions: Time warp is internal to the method; output is still evaluated at every original benchmark timestamp, with untouched references.
Phase targets use legal input/model evidence and no confirmation labels.
Endpoints, monotonicity, derivative regularity and interpolation error are checked; positive amplitude ridge lambda>0 ensures the profiled inverse is defined.
Input evidence may not distinguish timing from amplitude; then this is an identifiability boundary rather than a successful repair.
Thin amplitude QR requires full column rank; redundant phase directions are gauge, not automatically scientific ambiguity.
Principal-angle and noise formulas concern the unconstrained data problem; ridge regularization or active constraints changes the estimator.
Pointwise weighted Taylor remainder is stated only for block-diagonal weights.
method_expression: Jointly infer a small anchored monotone phase correction and amplitude correction; use the profiled formula only in the unconstrained phase regime; render outputs at original times.
distinguishing_prediction: Timing-dominated errors should respond to phase correction while amplitude-only shrinkage loses motion; amplitude-dominated errors should show the opposite pattern. In the unregularized local problem whitened target errors can be amplified by exactly 1/sqrt(kappa); ridge numerical solvability does not resolve zero-kappa data ambiguity.
falsifier: Reject if ordinary lag/alignment with equal evidence/budget is sufficient, or phase/amplitude remains unidentifiable on the native task.
closest_alternative: Classical phase-amplitude registration and Schur projection; simple lag correction, smoothing and displacement scaling.
decisive_comparison: Base, phase-only, amplitude-only and joint constrained repair with equal fitting/call budget; native CD-M/3D/4D at untouched timestamps and fresh confirmation. Qualify legal targets, gauges, rank, kappa and interpolation remainder before interpreting a decomposition; no evaluator timestamp changes.
operational_delta: Separates two competing mechanisms instead of interpreting every motion mismatch as coordinate noise; classical registration remains prior art.
feasibility_and_cost: Requires a qualified input/model motion target and a bounded nonlinear solve; target access and native method timing remain unresolved.
algebra_review_basis: Checked the Schur formula, active-inequality exception, nonidentifiability and second-order remainder. No relabeling of evaluation time.
empirical_status: Not implemented in this round; no native method comparison or outcome.
originality_status: Unadjudicated. Classical tools and historical related code are explicitly attributed.

revision.scope: Conditional mathematical and interface revision; no native experiment or implementation.
